name: Vagifem 10 µg
question: Does a 10-µg vaginal estradiol tablet improve vaginal atrophy signs and the most bothersome urogenital symptom compared with placebo?

design.population: Postmenopausal women aged 45 years or older with an intact uterus, at least three urogenital symptoms (one moderate to severe), vaginal pH above 5, and endometrial thickness below 4 mm.
design.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, pp 1054–1055

verdictNote: All three week-12 primary endpoint domains favored estradiol.
takeaway: In postmenopausal women with vaginal atrophy, 10-µg vaginal estradiol tablets improved vaginal cytology, vaginal pH grade, and most bothersome urogenital symptom scores more than placebo at 12 weeks.

reports.label: Placebo-controlled efficacy report
reports.citation: Simon J, Nachtigall L, Gut R, et al. Effective treatment of vaginal atrophy with an ultra-low-dose estradiol vaginal tablet. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2008;112(5):1053-1060. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e31818aa7c3
reports.followUp: Week-12 primary efficacy assessment; treatment continued through week 52
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and Methods, pp 1054–1055

results.measure: Week-12 change from baseline in vaginal epithelial cell proportions, intention-to-treat with last observation carried forward
results.note: Adjusted differences (estradiol minus placebo): parabasal −29 percentage points (95% CI −34.6 to −22.8); superficial +10 (6.2–13.8); intermediate +19 (12.3–25.0). Cytology differed after 2 weeks.

results.measure: Week-12 change from baseline in maturation value, intention-to-treat with last observation carried forward
results.note: Part of the vaginal cytology primary endpoint domain.

results.measure: Week-12 change from baseline in vaginal pH grade, intention-to-treat with last observation carried forward
results.note: The abstract reports a pH grade, not a measured pH-unit change; treatment effect differed from placebo after 2 weeks.
results.locator: Full text, Abstract, p 1053; Results, Table 2, p 1058

results.measure: Week-12 change from baseline in most bothersome symptom score, intention-to-treat with last observation carried forward
results.note: Treatment effect became apparent at week 4 and statistically significant at week 8; all efficacy treatment effects were significant at week 52.

results.measure: Week-12 change from baseline in vaginal health grade
results.locator: Full text, Abstract, p 1053; Results, pp 1057–1058

results.measure: Week-12 category, intention-to-treat with last observation carried forward
results.note: pH below 5.5 corresponded to no or mild atrophy; percentages use participants with pH data.

harms.label: Any adverse event
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 1058; 2010 Full text, Materials and Methods, p 877 (exposed placebo denominator)
harms.note: 777 events overall; most were mild or moderate.

harms.label: Serious adverse event
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 1058; 2010 Full text, Materials and Methods, p 877 (exposed placebo denominator)
harms.note: The estradiol group included one grade-2 endometrial adenocarcinoma.

harms.label: Withdrawal because of adverse event
harms.locator: Full text, Figure 1 and Results, p 1056

delivery.label: Treatment schedule
delivery.value: One assigned 10-µg estradiol or placebo vaginal tablet daily for 14 days, then twice weekly through 52 weeks; primary efficacy assessed at week 12.
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1055

delivery.label: 52-week completion
delivery.locator: Full text, Figure 1 and Results, p 1056

reports.label: Pooled 52-week endometrial safety
reports.citation: Simon J, Nachtigall L, Ulrich LG, et al. Endometrial safety of ultra-low-dose estradiol vaginal tablets. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2010;116(4):876-883. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e3181f386bb
reports.followUp: 52 weeks across the randomized estradiol cohort and a separate open-label safety cohort
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and Methods, pp 877–878

results.measure: Pooled 52-week hyperplasia or carcinoma incidence among evaluable endometrial biopsies, including events during treatment regardless of duration
results.note: Primary safety endpoint pooled 205 randomized estradiol recipients and 336 open-label recipients; no pooled randomized placebo comparison. Reported incidence and CI bounds met the paper's stated FDA and EMA thresholds.
results.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 878; Table 4 and Results, p 881

results.measure: Mean double-layer thickness at week 52 among completers
results.note: ANCOVA compared change from baseline; week-52 LOCF comparison P=0.654.
results.locator: Full text, Table 5 and Results, p 881

harms.label: Endometrial hyperplasia or carcinoma in pooled active-treatment cohorts
harms.locator: Full text, Table 4 and Results, pp 880–881
harms.note: One complex hyperplasia without atypia followed 9 days of exposure. One grade-2, stage-1B endometrioid adenocarcinoma followed 324 days of exposure and had no evaluable screening biopsy, so preexistence was uncertain.

delivery.label: Biopsy follow-up in pooled active-treatment cohorts
delivery.value: 541 estradiol recipients (205 randomized VAG-2195, 336 open-label VAG-1748); 456/541 (84.3%) completed the trials; 443 had a biopsy at week 52; 386 biopsy samples were included in the hyperplasia/carcinoma incidence analysis. Among 443 week-52 biopsies, 51 had no tissue and five had insufficient tissue with endometrial thickness at least 4 mm.
delivery.locator: Full text, Tables 2–4 and Results, pp 879–881
